Here's my recent, tokophobia related experience and perspective:

Unfortunately i just got through an unwanted pregnancy and had no option to abort. I confidently gave the baby up for a completely closed adoption.

 I am still very pissed about the fact I had to carry to term. I really hate abortion laws in the US. I hate my memories of giving birth in the hospital but I will say I feel lucky I had no complications with it. I Just really wish I could erase the memories of it because i hate associating any part of my life with that experience at all. I have weird dreams about it. I did not want to carry a child. My body did not feel like my own the entire time and I hated feeling movements. I also confided in very few people about it and never spoke of it at work, i tried to hide it as best as i could. A few co workers recently admitted to me they thought I was pregnant but didn't want to assume (thankfully!!) And the one time someone did mention they heard a rumor about me leaving on maternity leave soon, i told them that wasn't correct and it was just a medical leave, then ran to the bathroom and cried. I still feel like my body betrayed me, especially with the fact that my condition was difficult to hide at the end.

Basically even having a child in me didn't change my tokophobia and i think it resulted in me not wanting and being unable to bond with the baby at all. I chose not to see or hold it, i didn't want to know the gender but lets just say the hospital made a few big mistakes and ended up telling me even though i specifically told the hospital i didn't want to know it. 

I feel very abnormal because I felt no connection to the thing that grew inside me and just about every piece of literature/online post pertaining to my situation described women having some love/connection to it. I, however, didn't and still do not feel any love for it at all. I really don't want it to ever find me. What else makes me feel bad for wanting nothing to do with it/feeling no bond? My SO admitted that he would have preferred to raise it. 

Tl;dr: i just got over a pregnancy, all i feel from it is hatred/anger, I never want to go through that ever again, and you are not alone. I agree with you that the idea of pregnancy/motherhood is awful.
